classification.difficultyReason: The student recognises that the x≥0 half of the graph is f, then finds the quadratic from its roots plus one point (the y-intercept or the vertex). This is one reframing step and routine algebra, close to the 36-rated p24-q08 but with two parts.

content.prompt: Each graph shown is $y=f(|x|)$, where $f(x)$ is a quadratic. Find the equation of $f(x)$.

answer.worked:
The graph for $x\ge0$ is $y=f(x)$, so $f$ has zeros $1$ and $5$ and $f(0)=5$.
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=a(x-1)(x-5)\\5&=a(-1)(-5)\\a&=1\\f(x)&=(x-1)(x-5)\\f(x)&=x^2-6x+5\end{align*}$$

The graph for $x\ge0$ is $y=f(x)$, so $f$ has zeros $0$ and $6$ and passes through $(3,9)$.
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=ax(x-6)\\9&=a(3)(3-6)\\9&=-9a\\a&=-1\\f(x)&=-x(x-6)\\f(x)&=6x-x^2\end{align*}$$
